reference: Independent python re-derivation of the constant-gamma compressible-flow relations of NACA Report 1135 (isentropic, area-Mach, normal shock, theta-beta-M, Prandtl-Meyer), the Fanno and Rayleigh lines of Shapiro Vol. I, and the exact ideal-gas Riemann solver of Toro Ch. 4. Every relation is implemented twice by structurally different routes -- float64 closed forms with scipy brentq inversions, and a 60-digit mpmath second route that uses a different formulation wherever one exists (area ratio as a mass-flux ratio; the normal shock from raw mass/momentum/energy Rankine-Hugoniot balances; theta from the streamline density-ratio identity; Prandtl-Meyer and the Fanno friction function by numerical quadrature; Rayleigh T0/T0* assembled from p/p* and T/T*) -- and their mutual deviation is recorded as crosscheck. Spot-checked against the published NACA 1135 Table I and Table II entries.
reference_citations: Ames Research Staff, "Equations, Tables, and Charts for Compressible Flow", NACA Report 1135, 1953: eq.(44) isentropic, eq.(80) area ratio, eq.(93)-(99) normal shock, eq.(138) theta-beta-M, eq.(171a) Prandtl-Meyer. Verified against Table I (A/A*=1.6875 at M=2.000, A/A*=4.2346 at M=3.000, nu=26.380 deg at M=2.000) and Table II (M=2: M2=0.57735, p2/p1=4.5000, rho2/rho1=2.6667, T2/T1=1.6875, p02/p01=0.72087; M=3: M2=0.47519, p2/p1=10.333, rho2/rho1=3.8571, T2/T1=2.6790, p02/p01=0.32834).

A. H. Shapiro, "The Dynamics and Thermodynamics of Compressible Fluid Flow", Vol. I, Ronald Press, 1953, Ch. 6 (Fanno line: f_D L*/D, p/p*, T/T*, p0/p0*) and Ch. 7 (Rayleigh line: T0/T0*, p/p*, T/T*).

E. F. Toro, "Riemann Solvers and Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics", 3rd ed., Springer 2009, Ch. 4 (exact Riemann solver, eq. 4.5-4.9 pressure functions and eq. 4.51-4.56 wave speeds) and Table 4.1 (Sod problem: p*=0.30313, u*=0.92745, rho*L=0.42632, rho*R=0.26557).
provenance_note: Every one of the 235 closed-form cases carries a reference re-derived in python from NACA Report 1135, Shapiro Vol. I and Toro Ch. 4, implemented twice by structurally different routes and spot-checked against the published NACA 1135 Table I and Table II entries; no stored value was reused, so no case carries ref_source "recorded". The remaining 22 cases are not independent predictions and are labelled as such: the 4 unsteady-Euler cases assert conservation identities (mass and energy inventory drift, positivity repairs) plus a loose discretisation diagnostic, and the 18 nozzle internal-shock cases are a closure test -- the post-shock Mach, total-pressure loss, exit Mach and back pressure are re-derived from the pre-shock Mach the tool itself reports, so they prove the tool's internal-shock solution is self-consistent with the NACA 1135 relations, not that the shock is in the right place.
tolerance: Two surfaces are compared for every closed-form case. (1) The value the tool DISPLAYS, against the tool's own printed precision: |got-ref| <= 0.5*10^-d + 1e-9*|ref|, where d is the number of decimals the tool actually prints for that field (5 for the area-table state ratios, 4 for Mach and pressure ratios, 3 for angles and for Mach numbers printed by the nozzle, 2 for u* and for times in ms, 1 for temperatures and wave speeds). (2) The UNROUNDED value the tool publishes through Diagram.record.build().outputs for the four closed-form modules (area / Fanno / Rayleigh / oblique-P-M), at 1e-9 relative -- these are closed forms the tool inverts with >=90 bisections over a bracket of order unity, so 1e-9 is loose for the tool and tight for the reference, with one derived exception: at the Rayleigh thermal-choking point T0/T0* has a quadratic maximum, so inverting it for the exit Mach is a square-root problem in which one ulp of the target moves M by ~2e-8; for those 14 cases `record_tol` states that arithmetic bound and the exact, well-conditioned assertion T0/T0*(M_reported) = 1 is tested instead, to 1e-12. Regime, branch and status labels are compared as strings, and every control write is verified to have landed. For the unsteady Euler cases the criterion is conservation: mass and energy inventory drift must read zero to the resolution the tool prints (3 decimals of a percentage, |drift| <= 5e-4 %) over a run with transmissive boundaries and no wave reaching an end wall; the L1 pressure error against the exact Riemann solution is a discretisation diagnostic with a loose 5% bound, not a physics tolerance. For the nozzle internal-shock closure cases the reference is a band: the tool prints the pre-shock Mach number to 3 decimals, so that +-0.0005 is propagated through the closure chain and the tool value must fall inside the resulting interval.
distinct_result_note: 257 cases produced 257 distinct answer fingerprints (sha1 over every compared value plus the record outputs).

suggested_benchmark_entry.reference: Independent python re-derivation of the constant-gamma compressible-flow relations of NACA Report 1135 (isentropic, area-Mach, normal shock, theta-beta-M, Prandtl-Meyer), the Fanno and Rayleigh lines of Shapiro Vol. I, and the exact ideal-gas Riemann solver of Toro Ch. 4. Every relation is implemented twice by structurally different routes -- float64 closed forms with scipy brentq inversions, and a 60-digit mpmath second route that uses a different formulation wherever one exists (area ratio as a mass-flux ratio; the normal shock from raw mass/momentum/energy Rankine-Hugoniot balances; theta from the streamline density-ratio identity; Prandtl-Meyer and the Fanno friction function by numerical quadrature; Rayleigh T0/T0* assembled from p/p* and T/T*) -- and their mutual deviation is recorded as crosscheck. Spot-checked against the published NACA 1135 Table I and Table II entries.
citations: Ames Research Staff, "Equations, Tables, and Charts for Compressible Flow", NACA Report 1135, 1953: eq.(44) isentropic, eq.(80) area ratio, eq.(93)-(99) normal shock, eq.(138) theta-beta-M, eq.(171a) Prandtl-Meyer. Verified against Table I (A/A*=1.6875 at M=2.000, A/A*=4.2346 at M=3.000, nu=26.380 deg at M=2.000) and Table II (M=2: M2=0.57735, p2/p1=4.5000, rho2/rho1=2.6667, T2/T1=1.6875, p02/p01=0.72087; M=3: M2=0.47519, p2/p1=10.333, rho2/rho1=3.8571, T2/T1=2.6790, p02/p01=0.32834).

A. H. Shapiro, "The Dynamics and Thermodynamics of Compressible Fluid Flow", Vol. I, Ronald Press, 1953, Ch. 6 (Fanno line: f_D L*/D, p/p*, T/T*, p0/p0*) and Ch. 7 (Rayleigh line: T0/T0*, p/p*, T/T*).

E. F. Toro, "Riemann Solvers and Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics", 3rd ed., Springer 2009, Ch. 4 (exact Riemann solver, eq. 4.5-4.9 pressure functions and eq. 4.51-4.56 wave speeds) and Table 4.1 (Sod problem: p*=0.30313, u*=0.92745, rho*L=0.42632, rho*R=0.26557).
suggested_benchmark_entry.tolerance: Two surfaces are compared for every closed-form case. (1) The value the tool DISPLAYS, against the tool's own printed precision: |got-ref| <= 0.5*10^-d + 1e-9*|ref|, where d is the number of decimals the tool actually prints for that field (5 for the area-table state ratios, 4 for Mach and pressure ratios, 3 for angles and for Mach numbers printed by the nozzle, 2 for u* and for times in ms, 1 for temperatures and wave speeds). (2) The UNROUNDED value the tool publishes through Diagram.record.build().outputs for the four closed-form modules (area / Fanno / Rayleigh / oblique-P-M), at 1e-9 relative -- these are closed forms the tool inverts with >=90 bisections over a bracket of order unity, so 1e-9 is loose for the tool and tight for the reference, with one derived exception: at the Rayleigh thermal-choking point T0/T0* has a quadratic maximum, so inverting it for the exit Mach is a square-root problem in which one ulp of the target moves M by ~2e-8; for those 14 cases `record_tol` states that arithmetic bound and the exact, well-conditioned assertion T0/T0*(M_reported) = 1 is tested instead, to 1e-12. Regime, branch and status labels are compared as strings, and every control write is verified to have landed. For the unsteady Euler cases the criterion is conservation: mass and energy inventory drift must read zero to the resolution the tool prints (3 decimals of a percentage, |drift| <= 5e-4 %) over a run with transmissive boundaries and no wave reaching an end wall; the L1 pressure error against the exact Riemann solution is a discretisation diagnostic with a loose 5% bound, not a physics tolerance. For the nozzle internal-shock closure cases the reference is a band: the tool prints the pre-shock Mach number to 3 decimals, so that +-0.0005 is propagated through the closure chain and the tool value must fall inside the resulting interval.

findings.title: The unsteady-Euler module cannot be measured reproducibly through its own UI.
findings.detail: eulerAnim() advances the solution to a wall-clock target (eulerTStart + (now - eulerWallStart)/1000 * tEnd / replay) and advanceEulerTo() clips dt to that target, so the step sequence and the final field depend on frame timing. Pressing #eRun on the Sod case three times on the current build gives 270 / 276 / 278 steps and L1(p) = 1.98 / 1.99 / 1.99 % for first-order Godunov, and 412 / 415 / 415 steps and 0.17 / 0.16 / 0.17 % for the strong-shock MUSCL case; the same cases marched by the tool's own advanceEulerTo(tEnd) give 248 / 248 steps at 1.98 % and 399 / 399 steps at 0.17 %, identical every time. Not fixed here: it is a design property of an animated solver, not a wrong number, and both drift values stay far inside the 5 % discretisation bound. Reported so that no future benchmark grades this module through #eRun.

findings.title: Two different nozzle outputs collide on one record key, and one is silently lost.
findings.detail: gdStatsOf() (gasdynamics.html:1880) builds record keys with k.replace(/\s+/g,"_").replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_·/µ]/g,""), which strips every subscript. In the internal-shock and shock-at-exit regimes the stat labels "pₑ/p₀" and "p₀₂/p₀₁" both sanitise to "p/p", so the second overwrites the first. Reproduce: Ae/A* = 2.5, pb/p0 = 0.5663, air. The screen shows pₑ/p₀ = 0.5663 and p₀₂/p₀₁ = 0.6331; Diagram.record.build().outputs returns {"p/p": 0.6331, "Choke_p/p": 0.9608, "Design_p/p": 0.0640, "Shock_MM": "2.189 → 0.549"} - the exit pressure ratio is gone and the total-pressure ratio is standing under a key a reader will read as the exit ratio. recordCSV() (diagram-common.js:298) emits it as one row "outputs.p/p". The same sanitiser collapses "γ throat"/"γ exit" to "throat"/"exit" and, with the viscous panel on, "BL θ at throat" and "BL δ* at throat" both to "BL_at_throat". NOT a regression from the port: /root/site/gasdynamics.html:904 has the identical line. Not fixed in this pass: the one-line fix is to transliterate the sub/superscripts before stripping, but that renames record keys in the nozzle, shock-tube and Euler modules and therefore mutates a report and CSV artifact whose byte-level invariance the print/report pass certified across 56 documents on 2026-08-21. It belongs in a pass that can re-run repgate over the whole tree, not in an evidence refresh. It affects no number this benchmark grades.

findings.title: The oblique-shock Mach control declares a range narrower than the model enforces.
findings.detail: #oM carries max="12" while inputNum("oM", 2.5, 1.001, 100) accepts up to 100. Setting M1 = 50 leaves the field :invalid (checkValidity() === false) but the page computes and displays the constant-gamma answer with no warning: β = 90.000°, M2 = 0.3784, p2/p1 = 2916.5000. The answer is correct for the stated model and model.ranges does disclose "no real-gas, dissociation or condensation effects", so this is an inconsistency between the declared control range and the enforced model range, not an undisclosed extrapolation.

findings.title: A fixed 4-decimal format prints a small but nonzero total-pressure ratio as 0.0000.
findings.detail: At M1 = 50, gamma = 1.4 the oblique/normal-shock panel shows p₀₂/p₀₁ = "0.0000"; the true value is 1.1438e-6, and the record carries it correctly. The displayed figure reads as an exact zero total-pressure ratio, which is physically impossible. Same shape at M1 = 20 for all three gammas and in the Prandtl-Meyer p2/p1 near the vacuum limit. Cosmetic; the record is right.

findings.title: Numerical note: the Rayleigh exit Mach at thermal choking is only resolvable to ~2e-8.
findings.detail: T0/T0*(M) has a quadratic maximum at M = 1 (f''(1) = -1.3889 for gamma = 1.4), so inverting it at the choking point is a square-root problem: one ulp of the target moves M by sqrt(2u/|f''|) = 1.79e-8. The tool returns M_out = 0.9999999912848503 where the exact answer is 1, prints it correctly as 1.0000, and satisfies the exact relation T0/T0*(M_reported) = 1 to 0 - 1.5 ulp. This is the arithmetic, not the tool; the 14 affected cases carry a derived record_tol and are graded on the well-conditioned residual instead.
